Performers
Hans Duhan (baritone), Ferdinand Foll (piano) Documented

The label photograph of the scanned copy names Kammersänger Hans Duhan, baritone of the Vienna State Opera, with Prof. Ferdinand Foll at the piano; the Internet Archive description names the same two performers. Utz reports that Duhan recorded nineteen songs with Foll on 27 April, 2 May and 4 May 1928 and the remaining five (Nos. 16, 17, 19, 20, 23) with Lene Orthmann on 11 July 1928, so Orthmann does not play on this side. The Commons file description names only Duhan.

[3] [2] [4]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

Utz measures this song at 3:10 against a mean of 3:41 and describes a clear slowing in its second part. No source consulted states the key of the transfer; the transposition from the first edition and the absolute pitch are not established here.

[1] [2] [4]
Recorded
4 May 1928 Documented

The Internet Archive description of the disc that carries this side gives the recording date. Utz lists the same three Foll session days (27 April, 2 May and 4 May 1928) without assigning songs to days, so the song-by-day assignment rests on the Internet Archive uploader’s labelling. Commons gives only the year 1928.

[2] [4]
Place
Unknown Unknown

No source consulted names the studio or city of the session.

[2] [4]
Label
Gramola Record (The Gramophone Company (Czechoslovakia) Limited), as printed on the scanned copy Documented

The label photograph of this scanned copy shows a Gramola Record imprint, whereas the photographed first disc carries the His Master’s Voice imprint; the photographed copies of this set carry both imprints. The label gives no date, and nothing here dates the first issue or shows that the audio transfer derives from the photographed copy.

[2]
Catalogue
ER 276 Documented

The label photograph of the scanned copy prints Cat. No. ER 276, and the Commons file name agrees. The Internet Archive text description of the disc reads “ER 376”, which the photograph does not support; the discrepancy is the uploader’s.

[3] [1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
BK 2969, take 1 (run-out “Bk 2969” with I); side No. 24 (label number 942922); reverse side: Die Nebensonnen (matrix CL 4401-1; pianist Lene Orthmann, 11 July 1928). Disc 12 of 12 of the set; 25 cm. Documented

The label photograph of the scanned copy shows the matrix and take in the run-out; the Internet Archive description and the Commons file name give the same matrix and take. The set was issued as twelve discs, one song to a side (Utz). The photograph is of one copy and does not identify the copy from which the audio was transferred.

[3] [2] [1]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer engineer is named. The Commons file was uploaded on 11 August 2015 by the user Patachonf and re-uploaded on 10 and 15 February 2022 by the user Mitar; the Internet Archive item was added on 25 April 2019 by the uploader recordplayer78. These are upload facts, not transfer credits.

[1] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is identified. Upload dates are not treated as transfer dates.

[1] [2]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Both hosts hold a FLAC file. The Commons duration (195.50 s) and the Internet Archive FLAC length (195.41 s) agree within 0.15 s, which suggests the same digitisation; which host received it first is not established, and the source disc, stylus, equalisation and noise treatment are undocumented.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Both the music and the poem are out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Schubert died in 1828 and the poet Wilhelm Müller in 1827. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about any modern edition.

[6] [5] [7]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons applies PD-EU-audio to this recording, attributed to 1928. The Internet Archive item carries a Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL, which is the uploader’s assertion and is not treated as authority to waive any rights. The publication date of the original disc is not documented; the EU basis here depends on the recording being first published before 1963, which is inferred from its 1928 session. Not established as public domain in the United States.

  • PD-EU-audio — European performers’ and producers’ rights claimed expired.
  • Public Domain Mark 1.0 — licence URL on the Internet Archive item, uploader’s assertion.

Franz Schubert, Winterreise, No. 24, “Der Leiermann”, text by Wilhelm Müller; Hans Duhan, baritone, Ferdinand Foll, piano, 4 May 1928. Disc: matrix BK 2969. File via Wikimedia Commons (PD-EU-audio; territorial). Rights metadata: public domain in the EU only; no worldwide recording clearance is claimed. Rights statement
